evals.prompt: /make-skill a skill that writes a CHANGELOG entry from the commits since the last git tag, in Keep a Changelog format
evals.expected_output: A new .claude/skills/changelog-entry/ directory with a filled-in SKILL.md, a description that mentions changelog, release notes, and 'what changed since the last release', 2-3 test prompts in evals/evals.json, and a clean validator run.
expectations: A new skill directory exists under .claude/skills with a kebab-case name
SKILL.md has no leftover template comments
validate_skill.py reports no errors for the new skill
evals/evals.json contains at least two realistic prompts
The description names several phrasings a user might use, not just one keyword

evals.prompt: can you turn what we just did (running the linter, fixing the imports, then committing with a conventional commit message) into a skill i can reuse
evals.expected_output: Claude extracts the steps from the conversation, confirms them, scaffolds a skill (for example tidy-commit), and explains why each step is there rather than listing bare commands.
expectations: The skill body explains reasons for steps, not only commands
The skill is marked disable-model-invocation because it commits code

evals.prompt: the list-skills skill keeps printing paths I don't care about, tighten it up
evals.expected_output: Claude reads the existing list-skills SKILL.md and script, removes the path column or output, re-validates, and summarizes the change.
expectations: The existing skill is edited in place, not recreated under a new name
validate_skill.py reports no errors after the change
